evidence.detail: Swift enum descriptor 0x330c declares 11 payload and 13 empty cases; field descriptor 0x3710 agrees. Outer enum descriptor 0x3328 and its ABI-declared cached singleton accessor 0x17e4 establish the metadata passed to the exact libswiftCore runtime tag call at 0x14b4. Every incoming path to the outlined getter is dominated by that call and selects outer tag 0; reflection field 0x3850 directly references fixed enum descriptor 0x330c. Its static enum metadata 0x4330 points back to that descriptor and declares value-witness table 0x42b0, value size 156 and complete straight-line getEnumTag function 0x23fc. On every path the unchanged incoming outer object is copied at offset zero by the exact libSystem memcpy import into a fixed private frame interval of that size; no intervening unknown call or overlapping write is admitted. The getter called at 0x1538 targets 0x1844, either that declared getter or an equal complete straight-line body, and reads only that interval. Shared helper code never supplies enum identity or count. Its unchanged tag reaches the LDRSW index after an explicit 32-bit zero-extending write. Signed 32-bit entries at 0x1784 are added to 0x1554. REA+ restored computed edges, disassembled destinations and extended the owning function before observations; generated override labels are analysis metadata, not source/caller declarations. Under trusted-darwin-arm64-chkstk-v1, normal-return call at 0x14a8 binds exact ___chkstk_darwin from /usr/lib/libSystem.B.dylib (external 0x30, import slot 0x4010). X2/X8/X12/SP retain reaching values; other volatile registers, including X9/X10/X16/X17/X30, and flags remain unknown. The probe may read stack/thread state and fault; its 16-byte scratch write is [-288,-272) relative to function-entry SP, disjoint from admitted live private storage. limitations: High p-code is decompiler-derived, not original source or runtime behavior. is_dead preserves the Java AST flag; decoded block members can retain that flag, so block_membership separately reports actual syntax-tree membership.
Def-use links do not cross function boundaries and may omit memory aliasing, call side effects, or unresolved indirect flow.
Memory read/write effects include stack and temporary memory operations; they do not identify persistent state or business meaning.
Operation, input, and def-use limits can truncate large functions; inspect truncation, omitted lower bounds, and known omitted counts before drawing conclusions.
Known omitted-edge counts cover links omitted from retained operations; omitted operations may contain additional uncounted links.

The default profile requires Ghidra to report default auto-analysis complete; an explicitly bounded profile can admit a stable partial Program after its configured deadline. Every observation reports the measured analysis outcome.
The imported Program and temporary project are ephemeral and deleted on close. Annotation operations edit session database metadata; original executable bytes are never written.
Cancelling an active Ghidra request terminates its ephemeral database and discards session annotations. The selected target remains open; the next provider query imports the original artifact again.
Default-space addresses use lowercase 0x-prefixed hexadecimal; other address spaces use <percent-encoded-space>:0x<hex>.
References cover the complete Ghidra function-body AddressSet and exact entry. Dossier incoming edges omit sources owned by that function; procedure_references also retains those internal edges.
The dossier combines Ghidra FunctionManager, Listing, ReferenceManager, BasicBlockModel, and decompiler observations; provider-specific pseudocode and assembly are not cross-provider text invariants.

Resolved reference metadata identifies computed, indirect, external, call, jump, and data edges; unresolved targetless flows remain unknown, and function classifications distinguish thunks and externals.
Synthetic Ghidra entry-point references without actionable memory sources are omitted.
The Java bridge serializes one function request per Program and lets each decompilation run until it completes or the caller cancels.

evidence.detail: Swift enum descriptor 0x356c declares 11 payload and 13 empty cases; field descriptor 0x3970 agrees. Outer enum descriptor 0x3588 and its ABI-declared cached singleton accessor 0x1884 establish the metadata passed to the exact libswiftCore runtime tag call at 0x1580. Every incoming path to the outlined getter is dominated by that call and selects outer tag 0; reflection field 0x3ab0 directly references fixed enum descriptor 0x356c. Its static enum metadata 0x4218 points back to that descriptor and declares value-witness table 0x4198, value size 156 and complete straight-line getEnumTag function 0x249c. On every path the unchanged incoming outer object is copied at offset zero by the exact libSystem memcpy import into a fixed private frame interval of that size; no intervening unknown call or overlapping write is admitted. The getter called at 0x15d8 targets 0x18e4, either that declared getter or an equal complete straight-line body, and reads only that interval. Shared helper code never supplies enum identity or count. Its unchanged tag reaches the LDRSW index after an explicit 32-bit zero-extending write. Signed 32-bit entries at 0x1824 are added to 0x15f4. REA+ restored computed edges, disassembled destinations and extended the owning function before observations; generated override labels are analysis metadata, not source/caller declarations.

limitations: Case values are Swift ABI runtime tags, with payload cases before empty cases; field names are reflection metadata. Valid enum values supply the bound; this does not establish state reachability or original source order.
Control-flow recovery assumes the normal AArch64 ABI and private non-escaped frame storage. It does not execute the target or prove each case's high-level semantics.

evidence.detail: Swift enum descriptor 0x339c declares 11 payload and 13 empty cases; field descriptor 0x37a0 agrees. Under swift-dynamic-typed-snapshot-v1, the exact libswiftCore runtime tag call at 0x14f8 receives metadata from accessor 0x1864 for outer enum descriptor 0x33b8. Its source is the current SP after the last align16(N) allocation at 0x14dc, where N is VWT+64 of that same metadata value. The straight-line entry prefix proves only register/stack identities; unknown earlier calls and escapes are allowed and their memory history is discarded. Assumptions: a recursively valid active outer payload at this call's normal return; stable ABI metadata layout; ordinary nonwrapping, nonaliasing stack allocation with N<=align16(N), N large enough for the active payload; live source and destination until the child getter, and no asynchronous interference throughout the checked post-tag window through dispatch. Stable imported-call/GOT bindings throughout the prefix (no interposition or mutation by earlier unknown calls) are assumed; visible non-stack writes cannot establish probe effects. Every incoming path selects outer tag 1; direct reflection field 0x38ec binds inline offset-zero child descriptor 0x339c. Static child metadata 0x4338 declares VWT 0x42b8, size 156 and pure complete getter 0x247c. Complete inline SIMD byte origins prove destination byte j equals snapshot source byte j for all 156 bytes, with live/disjoint fixed destination and dynamic source. No unknown post-tag call/write, SP change, foreign entry or bypass is admitted. Getter call 0x153c reads that representation. A separate straight-line getter-return-to-dispatch proof rejects calls, SP changes, foreign/bypass entries and unmodeled stores, including effects on escaped tag spills. Shared helper code never supplies identity/count. This proof does not establish preceding copy/witness correctness, pre-tag nonescape, ownership/retention, or later lifetime semantics. Its unchanged tag reaches the LDRSW index after an explicit 32-bit zero-extending write. Signed 32-bit entries at 0x1804 are added to 0x1558. REA+ restored computed edges, disassembled destinations and extended the owning function before observations; generated override labels are analysis metadata, not source/caller declarations.

evidence.detail: Swift enum descriptor 0x332c declares 11 payload and 13 empty cases; field descriptor 0x3730 agrees. Outer enum descriptor 0x3348 and its ABI-declared cached singleton accessor 0x1804 establish the metadata passed to the exact libswiftCore runtime tag call at 0x14d4. Every incoming path to the outlined getter is dominated by that call and selects outer tag 0; reflection field 0x3870 directly references fixed enum descriptor 0x332c. Its static enum metadata 0x4330 points back to that descriptor and declares value-witness table 0x42b0, value size 156 and complete straight-line getEnumTag function 0x241c. On every path the unchanged incoming outer object is copied at offset zero by the exact libSystem memcpy import into a fixed private frame interval of that size; no intervening unknown call or overlapping write is admitted. The getter called at 0x1558 targets 0x1864, either that declared getter or an equal complete straight-line body, and reads only that interval. Shared helper code never supplies enum identity or count. Its unchanged tag reaches the LDRSW index after an explicit 32-bit zero-extending write. Signed 32-bit entries at 0x17a4 are added to 0x1574. REA+ restored computed edges, disassembled destinations and extended the owning function before observations; generated override labels are analysis metadata, not source/caller declarations. Under trusted-darwin-arm64-chkstk-v1, normal-return call at 0x14c8 binds exact ___chkstk_darwin from /usr/lib/libSystem.B.dylib (external 0x30, import slot 0x4010). X2/X8/X12/SP retain reaching values; other volatile registers, including X9/X10/X16/X17/X30, and flags remain unknown. The probe may read stack/thread state and fault; its 16-byte scratch write is [-288,-272) relative to function-entry SP, disjoint from admitted live private storage. evidence.detail: Swift enum descriptor 0x337c declares 11 payload and 13 empty cases; field descriptor 0x3780 agrees. Under swift-dynamic-typed-snapshot-v1, the exact libswiftCore runtime tag call at 0x14cc receives metadata from accessor 0x1858 for outer enum descriptor 0x3398. Its source is the current SP after the last align16(N) allocation at 0x14b0, where N is VWT+64 of that same metadata value. The straight-line entry prefix proves only register/stack identities; unknown earlier calls and escapes are allowed and their memory history is discarded. Assumptions: a recursively valid active outer payload at this call's normal return; stable ABI metadata layout; ordinary nonwrapping, nonaliasing stack allocation with N<=align16(N), N large enough for the active payload; live source and destination until the child getter, and no asynchronous interference throughout the checked post-tag window through dispatch. Stable imported-call/GOT bindings throughout the prefix (no interposition or mutation by earlier unknown calls) are assumed; visible non-stack writes cannot establish probe effects. Every incoming path selects outer tag 1; direct reflection field 0x38cc binds inline offset-zero child descriptor 0x337c. Static child metadata 0x4330 declares VWT 0x42b0, size 156 and pure complete getter 0x2470. Complete inline SIMD byte origins prove destination byte j equals snapshot source byte j for all 156 bytes, with live/disjoint fixed destination and dynamic source. No unknown post-tag call/write, SP change, foreign entry or bypass is admitted. Getter call 0x1530 reads that representation. A separate straight-line getter-return-to-dispatch proof rejects calls, SP changes, foreign/bypass entries and unmodeled stores, including effects on escaped tag spills. Shared helper code never supplies identity/count. This proof does not establish preceding copy/witness correctness, pre-tag nonescape, ownership/retention, or later lifetime semantics. Its unchanged tag reaches the LDRSW index after an explicit 32-bit zero-extending write. Signed 32-bit entries at 0x17f8 are added to 0x154c. REA+ restored computed edges, disassembled destinations and extended the owning function before observations; generated override labels are analysis metadata, not source/caller declarations.

limitations: Case values are Swift ABI runtime tags, with payload cases before empty cases; field names are reflection metadata. Valid enum values supply the bound; this does not establish state reachability or original source order.

evidence.detail: Swift enum descriptor 0x355c declares 11 payload and 13 empty cases; field descriptor 0x3960 agrees. Outer enum descriptor 0x3578 and its ABI-declared cached singleton accessor 0x1884 establish the metadata passed to the exact libswiftCore runtime tag call at 0x1580. Every incoming path to the outlined getter is dominated by that call and selects outer tag 1; reflection field 0x3aac directly references fixed enum descriptor 0x355c. Its static enum metadata 0x4218 points back to that descriptor and declares value-witness table 0x4198, value size 156 and complete straight-line getEnumTag function 0x249c. On every path the unchanged incoming outer object is copied at offset zero by the exact libSystem memcpy import into a fixed private frame interval of that size; no intervening unknown call or overlapping write is admitted. The getter called at 0x15d8 targets 0x18e4, either that declared getter or an equal complete straight-line body, and reads only that interval. Shared helper code never supplies enum identity or count. Its unchanged tag reaches the LDRSW index after an explicit 32-bit zero-extending write. Signed 32-bit entries at 0x1824 are added to 0x15f4. REA+ restored computed edges, disassembled destinations and extended the owning function before observations; generated override labels are analysis metadata, not source/caller declarations.

limitations: High p-code is decompiler-derived, not original source or runtime behavior. is_dead preserves the Java AST flag; decoded block members can retain that flag, so block_membership separately reports actual syntax-tree membership.
Def-use links do not cross function boundaries and may omit memory aliasing, call side effects, or unresolved indirect flow.
Memory read/write effects include stack and temporary memory operations; they do not identify persistent state or business meaning.
Operation, input, and def-use limits can truncate large functions; inspect truncation, omitted lower bounds, and known omitted counts before drawing conclusions.
Known omitted-edge counts cover links omitted from retained operations; omitted operations may contain additional uncounted links.

The default profile requires Ghidra to report default auto-analysis complete; an explicitly bounded profile can admit a stable partial Program after its configured deadline. Every observation reports the measured analysis outcome.
The imported Program and temporary project are ephemeral and deleted on close. Annotation operations edit session database metadata; original executable bytes are never written.
Cancelling an active Ghidra request terminates its ephemeral database and discards session annotations. The selected target remains open; the next provider query imports the original artifact again.

evidence.detail: Swift enum descriptor 0x337c declares 11 payload and 13 empty cases; field descriptor 0x3780 agrees. Under swift-dynamic-typed-snapshot-v1, the exact libswiftCore runtime tag call at 0x14e4 receives metadata from accessor 0x1850 for outer enum descriptor 0x3398. Its source is the current SP after the last align16(N) allocation at 0x14c0, where N is VWT+64 of that same metadata value. The straight-line entry prefix proves only register/stack identities; unknown earlier calls and escapes are allowed and their memory history is discarded. Assumptions: a recursively valid active outer payload at this call's normal return; stable ABI metadata layout; ordinary nonwrapping, nonaliasing stack allocation with N<=align16(N), N large enough for the active payload; live source and destination until the child getter, and no asynchronous interference throughout the checked post-tag window through dispatch. Stable imported-call/GOT bindings throughout the prefix (no interposition or mutation by earlier unknown calls) are assumed; visible non-stack writes cannot establish probe effects. Every incoming path selects outer tag 1; direct reflection field 0x38cc binds inline offset-zero child descriptor 0x337c. Static child metadata 0x4338 declares VWT 0x42b8, size 156 and pure complete getter 0x2468. Complete inline SIMD byte origins prove destination byte j equals snapshot source byte j for all 156 bytes, with live/disjoint fixed destination and dynamic source. No unknown post-tag call/write, SP change, foreign entry or bypass is admitted. Getter call 0x1528 reads that representation. A separate straight-line getter-return-to-dispatch proof rejects calls, SP changes, foreign/bypass entries and unmodeled stores, including effects on escaped tag spills. Shared helper code never supplies identity/count. This proof does not establish preceding copy/witness correctness, pre-tag nonescape, ownership/retention, or later lifetime semantics. Its unchanged tag reaches the LDRSW index after an explicit 32-bit zero-extending write. Signed 32-bit entries at 0x17f0 are added to 0x1544. REA+ restored computed edges, disassembled destinations and extended the owning function before observations; generated override labels are analysis metadata, not source/caller declarations.

limitations: Case values are Swift ABI runtime tags, with payload cases before empty cases; field names are reflection metadata. Valid enum values supply the bound; this does not establish state reachability or original source order.

Pre-tag nonescape, preceding copy/ownership and later lifetime semantics are not proved.

Its source is the current SP after the last align16(N) allocation at 0x14c0, where N is VWT+64 of that same metadata value. The straight-line entry prefix proves only register/stack identities; unknown earlier calls and escapes are allowed and their memory history is discarded. Assumptions: a recursively valid active outer payload at this call's normal return; stable ABI metadata layout; ordinary nonwrapping, nonaliasing stack allocation with N<=align16(N), N large enough for the active payload; live source and destination until the child getter, and no asynchronous interference throughout the checked post-tag window through dispatch. Stable imported-call/GOT bindings throughout the prefix (no interposition or mutation by earlier unknown calls) are assumed; visible non-stack writes cannot establish probe effects. Every incoming path selects outer tag 1; direct reflection field 0x38cc binds inline offset-zero child descriptor 0x337c. Static child metadata 0x4338 declares VWT 0x42b8, size 156 and pure complete getter 0x2468. Complete inline SIMD byte origins prove destination byte j equals snapshot source byte j for all 156 bytes, with live/disjoint fixed destination and dynamic source. No unknown post-tag call/write, SP change, foreign entry or bypass is admitted. Getter call 0x1528 reads that representation. A separate straight-line getter-return-to-dispatch proof rejects calls, SP changes, foreign/bypass entries and unmodeled stores, including effects on escaped tag spills. Shared helper code never supplies identity/count. This proof does not establish preceding copy/witness correctness, pre-tag nonescape, ownership/retention, or later lifetime semantics. Its unchanged tag reaches the LDRSW index after an explicit 32-bit zero-extending write. Signed 32-bit entries at 0x17f0 are added to 0x1544. REA+ restored computed edges, disassembled destinations and extended the owning function before observations; generated override labels are analysis metadata, not source/caller declarations.

limitations: Case values are Swift ABI runtime tags, with payload cases before empty cases; field names are reflection metadata. Valid enum values supply the bound; this does not establish state reachability or original source order.

swift-dynamic-typed-snapshot-v1: conditional on a recursively valid active outer value at the exact runtime tag call, stable ABI layout and imported-call/GOT bindings during the prefix (no interposition/mutation), live/disjoint stack regions, nonwrapping monotonic allocations and a stable checked post-tag window. Pre-tag nonescape, preceding copy/ownership and later lifetime semantics are not proved.

evidence.detail: Swift enum descriptor 0x338c declares 11 payload and 13 empty cases; field descriptor 0x3790 agrees. Under swift-dynamic-typed-snapshot-v1, the exact libswiftCore runtime tag call at 0x14f4 receives metadata from accessor 0x1860 for outer enum descriptor 0x33a8. Its source is the current SP after the last align16(N) allocation at 0x14d8, where N is VWT+64 of that same metadata value. The straight-line entry prefix proves only register/stack identities; unknown earlier calls and escapes are allowed and their memory history is discarded. Assumptions: a recursively valid active outer payload at this call's normal return; stable ABI metadata layout; ordinary nonwrapping, nonaliasing stack allocation with N<=align16(N), N large enough for the active payload; live source and destination until the child getter, and no asynchronous interference throughout the checked post-tag window through dispatch. Stable imported-call/GOT bindings throughout the prefix (no interposition or mutation by earlier unknown calls) are assumed; visible non-stack writes cannot establish probe effects. Under trusted-darwin-arm64-chkstk-v1 on normal return, prefix probe 0x14cc binds imported 0x32 from /usr/lib/libSystem.B.dylib through original applied chained GOT slot 0x4010; only X2/X8/X12/SP gain special preservation. Other volatile registers, flags and Swift-error X21 are killed. Its possible [symbolic-SP-16,symbolic-SP) scratch write is before the snapshot; all pre-tag memory facts are discarded. No allocation, nonfaulting execution or actual runtime binding is established. Every incoming path selects outer tag 1; direct reflection field 0x38dc binds inline offset-zero child descriptor 0x338c. Static child metadata 0x4340 declares VWT 0x42c0, size 156 and pure complete getter 0x2478. Complete inline SIMD byte origins prove destination byte j equals snapshot source byte j for all 156 bytes, with live/disjoint fixed destination and dynamic source. No unknown post-tag call/write, SP change, foreign entry or bypass is admitted. Getter call 0x1538 reads that representation. A separate straight-line getter-return-to-dispatch proof rejects calls, SP changes, foreign/bypass entries and unmodeled stores, including effects on escaped tag spills. Shared helper code never supplies identity/count. This proof does not establish preceding copy/witness correctness, pre-tag nonescape, ownership/retention, or later lifetime semantics. Its unchanged tag reaches the LDRSW index after an explicit 32-bit zero-extending write. Signed 32-bit entries at 0x1800 are added to 0x1554. REA+ restored computed edges, disassembled destinations and extended the owning function before observations; generated override labels are analysis metadata, not source/caller declarations.

limitations: Case values are Swift ABI runtime tags, with payload cases before empty cases; field names are reflection metadata. Valid enum values supply the bound; this does not establish state reachability or original source order.

Pre-tag nonescape, preceding copy/ownership and later lifetime semantics are not proved.

limitations: High p-code is decompiler-derived, not original source or runtime behavior. is_dead preserves the Java AST flag; decoded block members can retain that flag, so block_membership separately reports actual syntax-tree membership.
Def-use links do not cross function boundaries and may omit memory aliasing, call side effects, or unresolved indirect flow.
Memory read/write effects include stack and temporary memory operations; they do not identify persistent state or business meaning.
Operation, input, and def-use limits can truncate large functions; inspect truncation, omitted lower bounds, and known omitted counts before drawing conclusions.
Known omitted-edge counts cover links omitted from retained operations; omitted operations may contain additional uncounted links.

The default profile requires Ghidra to report default auto-analysis complete; an explicitly bounded profile can admit a stable partial Program after its configured deadline. Every observation reports the measured analysis outcome.
The imported Program and temporary project are ephemeral and deleted on close. Annotation operations edit session database metadata; original executable bytes are never written.
Cancelling an active Ghidra request terminates its ephemeral database and discards session annotations. The selected target remains open; the next provider query imports the original artifact again.
Default-space addresses use lowercase 0x-prefixed hexadecimal; other address spaces use <percent-encoded-space>:0x<hex>.
Ghidra auto-analysis state: analysis_complete=true; analysis_timed_out=false; analysis_timeout_seconds=60.
macOS sessions require a matching executable Ghidra native decompiler; REA+ checks for it but does not build native components or change Gatekeeper quarantine state.
